feedback.finish: Communication is all the different ways we share information with one another. For example, talking, writing letters and sending pictures or texts.

instruction.text: Now, let’s go way back to when cavemen were alive! Drag the handprint to the correct place to find out more.

feedback.finish: Instead of writing with letters and words, cavemen drew pictures to show events and beliefs.

instruction.text: What do cave paintings tell us? Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Cave paintings tell us what animals existed at the time.
Cave paintings tell us how early humans would work together to hunt for food.
Cave paintings tell us that early humans used simple shapes, patterns and handprints to communicate.

text: Some cave paintings have survived until today, communicating information to us tens of thousands of years after they were painted!

instruction.text: Thousands of years have passed, and we’re in ancient Egypt! Drag the eye to its place to find out more.

feedback.finish: Humans gradually developed more advanced forms of communication. One example is hieroglyphics, a written language that developed over thousands of years in ancient Egypt.

instruction.text: You are speaking to an Egyptian Pharaoh. Fill in the gaps.

hint.label: Pharaoh
hint.text: A Pharaoh was an Egyptian King or Queen.

atoms.b: We used hieroglyphs to write down important information and ((++stories shopping_lists)), where each symbol represented a word or sound.
They were also used to decorate tombs, like my one here! They helped ((++guide stop)) me to the afterlife.
Our ((++writing camera)) system was one of the first, and it later influenced the first alphabets, which eventually led to the one you use today!

feedback.finish: By combining symbols, Hieroglyphs could be used to make whole words and sentences.

instruction.text: Let’s jump forward to ancient Greece! Draw the letter E into the wax tablet to find out more.

feedback.finish: By now, humans had started using alphabets to communicate more clearly and quickly. Wax tablets were used to practise writing because the wax could be reused many times.

instruction.text: You are speaking to a messenger from ancient Greece. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: My job is to run from place to place delivering letters and ((++messages food)).
Sometimes, I even have to run between different ((++cities planets)), and it takes days!
It’s very hard ((++work fun)), but how else are people supposed to receive important messages?
